adds.title: Bangkok Post op-ed 2016 by Paisarn Likhitpreechakul, Sogi Foundation board member
adds.summary: By 8 September 2013 Thailand's Tourism Authority had launched the 'Go Thai Be Free' campaign to market Thailand as a pink/LGBT destination while same-sex marriage and civil union remained impossible, transgender men and women remained legally identified as their sex at birth with no gender-title change, and the Civil Partnership Bill after five reviews and public hearings in all four regions including a House Committee on Justice and Human Rights forum two months earlier remained off the House agenda after securing 20 MP signatures but only about 4,000 of the required 10,000 public signatures, leaving same-sex and transgender partners without spouse/partner inheritance, medical-care decision, and government spousal-benefit protections, so trans visitors receive tourist-oriented economic welcome and anonymity but not legal recognition or resident-equivalent rights.
